title: Constipation and Malaise
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with constipation, malaise, nausea, and vomiting. Occult blood is positive. Colon cancer is the third most common cancer and third most common cause of cancer mortality in the US. Left colon masses present with obstructive symptoms (constipation, decreased stool caliber); right colon masses present with iron deficiency anemia from occult bleeding. Workup: colonoscopy with biopsy for diagnosis (NOT just flexible sigmoidoscopy — must examine entire colon). CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast for staging (gold standard for metastasis screening). CEA level pre-op for prognosis and recurrence monitoring. Pre-op clearance: ECG, PT/PTT, type and screen, NPO. Treatment: surgical resection (colectomy) by colorectal surgery. If lymph node positive → adjuvant chemotherapy. Follow-up: CEA q3-6mo, CT annually x 5yr, colonoscopy at 1yr then q3yr.

stacks.finding: Carcinoembryonic antigen — pre-op prognostic marker and monitors recurrence. Post-op CEA <2-3 = good prognosis.

physical_exam.abdominal: May have mass on palpation. Distension possible with obstruction.
physical_exam.skin: Pallor if iron deficiency anemia present.

decoys.label: Flexible sigmoidoscopy
decoys.reason_wrong: Does not cover enough colon to verify absence of polyps/cancer. Full colonoscopy is required before surgery for colon cancer.

decoys.label: PET scan as solo staging
decoys.reason_wrong: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast is gold standard for metastasis screening. PET provides no supplemental information beyond CT.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Full colonoscopy examines entire colon. Biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma. Left colon = obstruction symptoms; Right colon = IDA from occult bleeding.
Gold standard for colorectal cancer metastasis screening. Determines resectability.
Tumor marker. Elevated pre-op. Post-op normalization (<2-3) = good prognosis. Rising CEA suggests recurrence/liver mets.
Curative intent. Adjuvant chemo if lymph node positive. Follow-up colonoscopy at 1 year then q3yr.

case_summary: Colon adenocarcinoma. Constipation + malaise + positive FOBT. Colonoscopy with biopsy → CT staging → CEA → pre-op labs → NPO → colectomy. Office → surgery. 90% recurrences within 3 years — close follow-up essential.
